abstract: BACKGROUND: The presence of liver metastases represents an independent poor risk prognostic factor for survival in patients with germ cell tumors. METHODS: The clinical files of 37 patients who had undergone liver resection for the treatment of disseminated germ cell tumors were reviewed to define the indications for resection of residual liver metastases after chemotherapy in patients with germ cell tumors. The histologic patterns of primary tumor and residual disease were compared. The prognostic factors for survival were studied by univariate analysis. RESULTS: All but 2 of 37 patients underwent complete resection. One patient died of postoperative complications. Thirteen complications occurred in 10 patients. Twelve patients had active residual tumor, 7 patients had mature teratoma, and 18 patients had only necrosis on histologic examination. Twenty-three of 37 patients (62%) were alive with no evidence of disease after a median follow-up of 66 months (range, 31-134 months). Three prognostic factors were found to be significant in the univariate analysis for unfavorable outcome: the presence of pure embryonal carcinoma in the primary tumor, liver metastases measuring > 30 mm in greatest dimension at the time of surgery, and the presence of viable, active residual disease. CONCLUSIONS: Because it is impossible to determine the histologic pattern of residual liver masses after chemotherapy with current imaging tools and percutaneous biopsy, patient selection for liver surgery may be undertaken according to the size of residual liver masses. Patients with masses that measure < or = 10 mm in greatest dimension should be considered for close follow-up, because they have a high probability of necrosis and are at low risk for malignant disease. Male patients with masses that measure > or = 30 mm in greatest dimension represent a high-risk group of patients who are not likely to benefit from liver surgery. Only male patients with masses that measure 10-29 mm in greatest dimension and all female patients with masses that measure > 10 mm in greatest dimension should be considered for liver resection.
abstract_ja: 背景：播種性胚細胞腫瘍の患者において、肝転移の存在は生存に関する独立した予後不良因子である。方法：播種性胚細胞腫瘍に対する肝切除を受けた37例の診療記録を後方視的に検討し、化学療法後の残存肝転移に対する切除の適応を明らかにすることを目的とした。原発巣と残存病変の組織像を比較した。生存に関する予後因子を単変量解析により検討した。結果：37例中35例が完全切除を受けた。1例が術後合併症で死亡した。10例に計13件の合併症が生じた。12例に活動性の残存腫瘍が、7例に成熟奇形腫が、18例に壊死のみが組織学的に認められた。追跡期間中央値66か月（範囲31～134か月）で、23例（62%）が病勢の認められない状態で生存していた。単変量解析で予後不良因子として有意であったのは、原発巣の純粋な胎児性癌、手術時に最大径30 mmを超える肝転移、および活動性の残存病変の存在の3因子であった。結論：化学療法後の残存肝腫瘤の組織像は現行の画像検査や経皮生検では判別できないため、肝切除の症例選択は腫瘤の大きさに基づいて行われることがある。最大径10 mm以下の腫瘤は壊死である可能性が高く悪性の危険は低いため、綿密なフォローアップを検討すべきである。男性で最大径30 mm以上の腫瘤を有する患者は高リスク群であり、肝切除の利益を受ける可能性は低いと考えられる。最大径10～29 mmの男性患者、および最大径10 mmを超える女性患者のみが肝切除を検討すべきである。
